title: WPSB/770/2024 of MAIRAJ HUSSAIN Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Service Bench No.770 of 2024
Mairaj Hussain and Another --Petitioners
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand and Others --Respondents
------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:
Mr. Anil Bisht, learned counsel for petitioners.
Mr. Sushil Vashisth, learned Standing Counsel with Mr. Prem
Prakash Bhatt, learned Brief Holder for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondent Nos.1 to 3.
Mr. Piyush Tiwari, learned counsel for respondent No.4.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Coram: Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J. (Oral)
 Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Petitioner has challenged the judgment dated
06.09.2024 passed by Uttarakhand Public Service
Tribunal in Claim Petition No.54/NB/DB,2022. By the
said judgment, Claim Petition filed by respondent No.4
(Anuj Jain), challenging the order dated 02.02.2022, was
allowed.
2. By the order dated 02.02.2022 passed by Chief
Engineer, Irrigation Department, Anuj Jain (respondent
No.4) was downgraded in the Seniority List of Junior
Engineers from S.No.119 to 173-A. Operative portion of
the judgment dated 06.09.2024 is extracted below:-
"24. The petition is disposed of in terms of judgment
rendered by the Tribunal on 29.11.2022 in claim petition
no.114/DB/2022 Manu Kumar vs. State of Uttarakhand
and others, which has been upheld by the Hon'ble High
Court of Uttarakhand, SLP against which has been
dismissed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
25. Seniority list, in the instant case, shall abide by
the aforesaid decisions."
3. Learned counsel for petitioners submits that
petitioners were appointed as Junior Engineer
(Mechanical) by direct recruitment on the
recommendation of Uttarakhand Public Service

UKHC010198262024
2026:UHC:7251-DB
2
Commission during Recruitment Year 2013-14, while
Anuj Jain (respondent No.4), who was initially appointed
as Junior Clerk in Irrigation Department on 21.03.1998,
was promoted as Junior Engineer on 24.05.2014 against
the promotion quota available to ministerial employees
during the same Recruitment Year i.e. 2013-14. He
contends that respondent No.4 obtained Diploma in
Mechanical Engineering only on 12.11.2013, as is
apparent from the Diploma Certificate issued to him by
Indira Gandhi National Open University (annexed as
Annexure No.3 to the writ petition), and is admitted in
Para 5 of the counter affidavit filed by State Government
before the Tribunal; since Diploma in Mechanical
Engineering is essential for promotion from ministerial
post to the post of Junior Engineer and respondent No.4
was not educationally qualified for such promotion on the
first date of the year of Recruitment Year i.e. 01.07.2013,
therefore, respondent No.4 could not have been
considered for promotion during Recruitment Year 2013-
14. Thus, he submits that respondent No.4 was ineligible
and was wrongly promoted during Recruitment Year
2013-14, and he was also wrongly placed above
petitioners in the seniority list.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent
No.4 submits that since order of promotion issued in
favour of his client has not been disturbed and the fact
remains that respondent No.4 was promoted as Junior
Engineer on 24.05.2014, therefore, as a natural corolary,
he is entitled to seniority from the date of his order of
substantive appointment on the post of Junior Engineer,
and by application of rota-quota rule, he is entitled to be
placed above the petitioners, who are directly recruited
Junior Engineers.

UKHC010198262024
2026:UHC:7251-DB
3
5. To buttress his argument, learned counsel for
respondent No.4 submits that promotion given to
respondent No.4 was not ad-hoc or temporary, but it was
a regular promotion on the recommendation of DPC,
therefore, he is entitled to seniority from the date of his
regular promotion. He further submits that Rule 8 of
Uttarakhand Government Servants (Determination of
Seniority) Rules, 2002, provides that where during the
course of same recruitment year, recruitment is made
both by direct recruitment and by promotion, then the
promottee will be placed above direct recruitee. Thus, he
submits that respondent No.4 was rightly placed above
the petitioners in final seniority list prepared on
14.02.2018.
6. Learned counsel for respondent No.4 further
submits that petitioners never raised objection before
Competent Authority against the promotion or seniority
given to respondent No.4 and they also did not
participate in the proceedings before learned Tribunal,
even though notices were sent to them. He further
submits that respondent No.4 has earned as many as
three promotions, namely, (i) Junior Engineer (ii)
Additional Assistant Engineer and (iii) Assistant
Engineer, and learned Tribunal rightly decided the claim
petition in his favour.
7. This Court do not find any reason to interfere
with the judgment rendered by learned Tribunal.
Respondent No.4 was promoted as Junior Engineer on
24.05.2014 and he was given seniority from that date
and was placed at S.No.119 in the Seniority List. Without
disturbing the promotion given to respondent No.4
effective from 24.05.2014, his seniority could not be

UKHC010198262024
2026:UHC:7251-DB
4
disturbed. The show-cause notice issued to respondent
No.4 on 11.12.2021 was in the right earnest, whereby, he
was informed that he became eligible for promotion to the
post of Junior Engineer during recruitment year 2014-15
only, while he was promoted against a vacancy during
recruitment year 2013-14, however, instead of
proceeding in that direction, Competent Authority chose
to downgrade respondent No.4 in the seniority list,
without correcting his date of promotion.
8. We find force in the submission made by
learned counsel appearing for respondent No.4 that
without correcting the date of promotion of respondent
No.4, his seniority cannot be disturbed.
9. For the aforesaid reasons, we do not find any
scope for interference with the impugned order.
Accordingly, the writ petition fails and is dismissed.
10. Pending application stands disposed of.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
